purpose: The hand adjudication of every record the portfolio-transfer scanner flags, so that the count in the manuscript rests on an inspectable record rather than on the assertion that the flags were checked. Each entry gives the filing's own words, the direction, whether the arrangement is a discrete transaction or a standing one, and what it means for the record's development triangle.
round: round 56 (R166, corrected by R169, R170, R174, R175, R180, R181, R185, R186); updated after R194 and R199-R203, and R198 settled; R221 (frozen review of 21 September 2026, M02) added four rescan flags and 1856/2020
why_standing_and_discrete_are_both_flagg: An adversarial review of 11 September 2026 asked whether four of these (1971/2021-2023, 6133/2021) are a standing annual treaty rather than a one-off transfer, and whether the scanner's own exclusion of ordinary quota share ought to catch them. The distinction is real and is recorded per record below, but it does not change the flag. What the paper needs to know is whether a syndicate's gross development triangle carries movement that is not its own re-estimation of its own older years. A treaty that assumes a prior year's run-off every year contaminates the triangle every year; that it does so on a standing basis makes the contamination more regular, not less real. The exclusion the scanner applies is to quota share of CURRENT business, which is a different thing.
directions_matter: An inward transfer adds another syndicate's older liabilities to this triangle, so its diagonal is not this syndicate's own development: 2008/2021's provisions note carries the Hiscox take-on inside 'change in prior year provisions'. What an outward transfer does depends on its form. One that moves the liabilities themselves -- a reinsurance to close out, a Part VII transfer, a novation of the policies -- takes them off the gross triangle. One that is reinsurance -- an outward loss portfolio transfer or quota share -- leaves the gross liabilities with the syndicate, which still owes them, and changes only its net position, so it does not contaminate a gross triangle at all.

also_in_the_ritc_regime.meaning: these records are themselves the ASSUMING party of a reinsurance to close, so the model's RITC regime already treats their diagonal as carrying assumed business. A record that merely mentions an RITC it ceded is not counted here: 1971/2021 cedes its 2019 year into 1969 and is not in this list.

field_meanings.also_accepts_ritc: true when the syndicate is the party ACCEPTING a reinsurance to close, not merely when its filing mentions one
field_meanings.direction: inward adds another syndicate's older liabilities to this triangle; outward removes them; both means the filing shows each in the same year
field_meanings.arrangement: discrete is a dated transaction; standing is an arrangement that repeats annually under one agreement

withdrawn_by_R221.why: R200 filed it as a quota share of Syndicate 1955's current business; the p6 sentence records 15.4% of 1955's 2015-and-prior reserves transferred into 1856's 2016 year of account, and it is now a genuine record

what_this_does_not_settle: Nothing in this register is a modelling decision. The one taken on it is recorded in PLAN R195: on 13 September 2026 the owner decided that confirmed inward transfers, flagged or found by hand, are treated like RITC.

Whether any transfer went undetected is not measured as a rate. R198 read by hand the records whose events name a transfer in a strong-evidence sentence but are not flagged, and six named records; that found 3500/2018, which neither scanner flags. The scanners read the vocabulary they know: adverse development cover and retrospective reinsurance are not transfer terms in it.

How much of the corpus is affected. This is a count of flagged reports. It is not weighted by the size of the syndicates involved, and no size metric is applied here, so nothing in this file supports a statement that the affected share is large or small.
how_the_quotes_were_taken: Each `filing_says` is trimmed from the sentence the scanner captured from the filing's text layer, and checked against the scanner's own snippet -- not re-read from the page image. So these quotes verify the scanner's reading of the filing, which is a weaker claim than verifying the filing. An OCR misread the scanner made would be reproduced here. Where a direction or an amount turns on the wording, the sentence is quoted in full rather than trimmed.
directions_matter_correction: The first version said every outward transfer removes liabilities from the triangle, which is true only of the first kind. Most outward transfers the scanner finds are the second kind (1861/2021 with RiverStone, 1967/2020 ceded to BIC, 2001/2018 purchased), and under the old sentence each would have read as gross contamination.
